title: Can you play a provisional ball if your ball is in a penalty area?
question: If you think your ball might be in a penalty area (like a water hazard), can you play a provisional ball?

choices.text: Yes, you must always play a provisional ball.
No, you are not allowed to play a provisional ball in this case.
Only if your ball is in long grass.
Yes, but only after searching for 5 minutes.

explanation: A provisional ball cannot be played if it is known or virtually certain your ball is in a penalty area. Instead, you must follow the penalty area rules.

juniorVersion.title: Can you hit a second ball if your ball might be in the water or a penalty area?
juniorVersion.question: If you hit your ball and think it might be in a pond or a penalty area, can you hit another ball just in case?

choices.text: Yes, you always need to hit another (provisional) ball.
No, you cannot hit another ball if it might be in the water or penalty area.
Only if your ball went into tall grass.
Yes, but only after looking for 5 minutes.

juniorVersion.explanation: You cannot play a provisional ball if your ball might be in a pond or penalty area. You have to use the penalty area rules instead.

vocabulary.simpleMeaning: A second ball you play if you think your first ball might be lost or out of bounds.
An area on the course like a pond or stream, marked with red or yellow lines or stakes.

juniorVersion.teachingTip: Show children where penalty areas are marked on the course. Let them practise dropping balls and talk about what to do if their ball goes into water.
likelyMisconceptions: Thinking you can always hit a provisional ball if you can't see your ball.
Not knowing you have to follow different rules for balls in penalty areas.
